- Model tends to overestimate prices in early forecast periods, especially after sharp spikes or recovery phases.
- Forecasts often peak too early or too high during upward momentum, then fail to adjust downward as prices mean-revert.
- Model underestimates true price levels during sustained upward trends, particularly when recent history shows strong momentum.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in the first 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, suggesting lag or delayed response to new data.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values when recent history includes high volatility or outlier spikes.
- When true prices show strong downward correction after a peak, model fails to anticipate the drop, leading to overestimation in subsequent periods.
- Model underreacts to low-price periods, often failing to recognize when prices are approaching support levels.
- Forecasts should be adjusted downward if recent 7–14 day average is below 70% of the 30-day moving average.
- Model overestimates volatility in early periods, leading to over-optimistic price peaks.
- When true prices show a clear downward trend after a spike, model should reduce forecast by 5–10% for the next 3–5 days.
